title: Multi-Expert Seizure Annotation
description: Stereotactic EEG recordings of 78 seizures (44 spontaneous, 34 stimulation-induced) from 29 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy, recruited at the University of Pennsylvania and the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia. Three or five board-certified epileptologists independently annotated each seizure for onset time, onset channels, and channels seizing 10 seconds after onset. The BIDS-formatted data include electrode localizations, patient demographics, and clinical outcomes. They support benchmarking of automated seizure onset and spread detection against expert performance and comparison of spontaneous and stimulation-induced seizure networks.
methods_description: Recordings were acquired with a Natus Quantum system at 512-2048 Hz using sEEG depth electrodes (Ad-Tech, PMT or DIXI). Stimulation-induced seizures used bipolar biphasic stimulation (HUP: 1 Hz, 3 mA, 300 or 500 µs; CHOP: 1-8 mA, 1-2 Hz, 300-500 µs). Each seizure was annotated by multiple epileptologists following a standardized protocol. Electrodes were localized by co-registering post-implant CT to pre-implant MRI, with Desikan-Killiany parcellation in FreeSurfer.
